mainTopic: Which מצוות partners owe according to רבי אלעאי, and how far ראשית הגז is compared to תרומה
overview: The גמרא explains why partners still owe several מצוות, even though רבי אלעאי exempts partners from ראשית הגז. For מזוזה, מעשר, ביכורים, ציצית and מעקה, a פסוק says 'your' in the singular, but another word shows that partners are included. Each singular word then gets its own job, like leaving out a partnership with a גוי, produce from outside ארץ ישראל, a borrowed טלית, or a בית כנסת. For מתנות כהונה, the גמרא concludes that partners' duty is learned from תרומה, and זובחי הזבח teaches that the כהן collects from the butcher. Then רב ביבי בר אביי and רב חנינא מסורא reject these rules, showing from ברייתות that רבי אלעאי also exempts partners from בכורה, מתנות and even תרומה. A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעאי limits מתנות and ראשית הגז to ארץ ישראל, and רבא explains that he learns ראשית הגז from תרומה through the shared word 'giving.' אביי tests how far this comparison goes: some rules of תרומה do not carry over to wool, but the ban on giving from new for old does. The amud ends with אביי challenging the comparison from our משנה about buying a גוי's sheep, and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: מזוזה goes on the right side, the way you enter
steps.stepSummary: The word ביתך is read as ביאתך, 'your entering.' It teaches that the מזוזה goes on the right side, since a person steps in with the right foot first.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your house' means 'the way you enter.' So the מזוזה goes on the right side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the word ביתך in the מזוזה פסוק does not exempt partners. That word is used to teach which side of the doorway gets the מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think ביתך ('your house,' one owner) leaves out a house owned by partners. The גמרא answers that the word is needed for something else: reading it as ביאתך shows the מזוזה goes on the right, the side you naturally enter with. Since the word is used up for this lesson, it cannot be used to exempt partners.

steps.title: Partners owe tithes because of a plural word
steps.stepSummary: The singular phrase מעשר דגנך might exempt partners, but the plural מעשרותיכם includes them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for tithes: even though it says 'the tithe of your grain,' which suggests only your own grain and not grain shared with a partner, the Torah also wrote 'your tithes' in the plural.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why partners must still separate מעשר, even though one פסוק uses the singular word 'your.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular דגנך could mean a single owner only. The plural מעשרותיכם ('your tithes,' many of you) shows that grain owned by several people is also obligated.

steps.title: So what is 'your grain' teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If partners are obligated, the גמרא asks what the singular word דגנך comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what does 'the tithe of your grain' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what purpose the word דגנך serves, now that it does not exempt partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not use extra words for nothing. Since דגנך is not excluding partners, it must be teaching something else.

steps.title: It excludes grain shared with a gentile

steps.deeperAnalysis: So both words have a job. מעשרותיכם brings in partnerships between Jews, and דגנך ('yours,' a Jew's) leaves out a partnership with a גוי.

steps.title: Gifts to the כהן: the word 'and he shall give'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up מתנות כהונה, where the singular word ונתן might suggest one owner only.
steps.simpleTranslation: The gifts to the כהן: even though the Merciful One wrote 'and he shall give.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the case of מתנות (the foreleg, jaw and stomach given to a כהן). This line sets up the next move: why partners are still obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Partners owe the מתנות, even though ונתן ('he shall give') is singular. The singular word by itself is not the real problem, though. It sets up a גזירה שוה that comes next.

steps.title: A possible link to the first sheared wool
steps.stepSummary: One could learn 'giving' here from 'giving' by ראשית הגז. Since partners are exempt there, they would be exempt from מתנות too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One could say: learn 'giving' from 'giving' by the first sheared wool. Just as there, partners are not obligated, so too here, partners are not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a reason why partners might be exempt from מתנות: a word link to ראשית הגז, where רבי אלעאי exempts partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, 'giving,' appears in both מצוות. That word link (a גזירה שוה) would carry the exemption for partners from ראשית הגז over to מתנות.

steps.title: 'Those who slaughter' is plural, so partners owe
steps.stepSummary: The plural phrase זובחי הזבח shows that partners who slaughter together must give the מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One wrote 'from those who slaughter an animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plural phrase 'those who slaughter' includes partners, so the word link does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זובחי ('those who slaughter') is plural, which means more than one owner. A clear plural word in the פסוק itself is stronger than the גזירה שוה, so partners are obligated in מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who slaughter an animal (plural)

steps.whatToRemember: Partners are exempt from ראשית הגז (according to רבי אלעאי), but they owe מעשר and מתנות. Steps 8-11 refine where the duty of מתנות really comes from.

phrases.english: The Merciful One wrote 'from those who slaughter the animal.'

steps.title: Why learn from first shearing and not from תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that, without זובחי הזבח, we would compare מתנות כהונה to ראשית הגז. It says we should compare them to תרומה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wait: is the only reason partners must give the מתנות that the תורה wrote 'those who slaughter' in the plural? Without that, would we really have learned from first shearing? Just the opposite: we should learn from תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from Step 7. It says the comparison to ראשית הגז was never the obvious one, because תרומה is an equally good, or better, model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 assumed that the word 'giving' links מתנות to ראשית הגז, where partners are exempt. But 'giving' also appears by תרומה, where partners are obligated. So the default should be that partners are obligated, and the plural זובחי הזבח would not be needed for that.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees: learn from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge. Partners' obligation in מתנות is indeed learned from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge is correct. Partners are obligated in מתנות because we learn from תרומה. This admission sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the obligation comes from תרומה, the plural זובחי הזבח is no longer needed for partners. That opens a new problem, which comes in the next step.

steps.title: So why does the תורה say 'those who slaughter'?
steps.stepSummary: If the obligation comes from תרומה, what is the phrase זובחי הזבח for?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then why do I need the words 'from those who slaughter an animal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what job the phrase זובחי הזבח now does, since it is no longer needed to obligate partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that no words in the תורה are extra. Since the partnership rule now comes from תרומה, this phrase must teach something else.

steps.title: It teaches רבא's rule: claim from the butcher
steps.stepSummary: זובחי הזבח teaches the ruling of רבא that the כהן's claim to the gifts is against the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes for the ruling of רבא, who said: the claim is against the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase teaches who the כהן goes to for his gifts: the one who slaughters, the butcher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'slaughterers' points to the person doing the slaughtering. The כהן may claim the gifts from the butcher even if the animal belongs to someone else. This does not exempt a buyer who has the gifts from handing them over.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim is against the butcher

steps.whatToRemember: Partners must give מתנות כהונה, learned from תרומה. The phrase זובחי הזבח teaches that the כהן collects from the butcher.

steps.stepSummary: Even though the פסוק about ביכורים says 'your land' in the singular, another פסוק says 'their land' in the plural, so partners must bring ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ביכורים: even though it is written 'your land', which would suggest yours yes, a partnership no, the תורה also wrote 'the first fruits of all that is in their land'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new מצוה‎, ביכורים, and applies the same singular-versus-plural pattern. A plural word in another פסוק shows that partners are obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular ארצך could have exempted land owned in partnership. The plural בארצם from a different פסוק overrides that and includes partners.

steps.title: Jointly owned garments still need ציצית
steps.stepSummary: Even though the פסוק says 'your covering' in the singular, another פסוק says 'their garments' in the plural, so a garment owned by partners needs ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: ציצית: even though the תורה wrote 'your covering,' which suggests only your own garment and not a shared one, the תורה also wrote 'on the corners of their garments throughout their generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same pattern it used for ביכורים to ציצית. One פסוק sounds singular, but another פסוק in the plural shows that partners are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כסותך ('your covering') could make us think only a garment owned by one person needs ציצית. The plural בגדיהם ('their garments') in another פסוק includes garments owned by several people together. So shared ownership does not exempt a garment.

steps.title: 'Your covering' teaches that a borrowed טלית is exempt for thirty days

steps.title: A jointly owned roof still needs a מעקה
steps.stepSummary: Even though the פסוק says 'your roof' in the singular, the phrase 'if anyone falls from it' shows that partners must also build a railing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעקה: even though the תורה wrote 'for your roof,' which suggests only your own roof and not a shared one, the תורה also wrote 'if anyone falls from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same pattern to the מצוה of building a railing around a roof. A roof owned by partners still needs one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular לגגך ('for your roof') could suggest that only a roof owned by one person needs a railing. But the reason given in the פסוק is danger: 'if anyone falls from it.' That danger is the same on a shared roof, so partners are obligated too.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question as before: what is the singular word for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'your roof' does not exclude partners, it must have another purpose. The גמרא is setting up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Your roof (singular)
'What does it come for?', asking what a word teaches

phrases.english: But then, what does "your roof" come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the singular word, now that Step 18 showed it does not exclude partners.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the singular גגך teaches if it does not exclude jointly owned roofs.

steps.title: 'Your roof' excludes synagogues and study halls
steps.stepSummary: גגך teaches that בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות are not obligated in מעקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the singular 'your roof' leaves out synagogues and study halls from the obligation of מעקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your roof' means a roof that belongs to you. Synagogues and study halls are not anyone's private house, so the word 'your' leaves them out. This is the same pattern as the earlier answers: the singular word gets a new job.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out of the rule
Synagogues
Houses of Torah study

steps.whatToRemember: Each time, the plural or general wording includes partners, and the singular 'your' teaches a different exclusion: produce from outside ארץ ישראל for ביכורים, a borrowed garment for ציצית, and synagogues and study halls for מעקה.

phrases.english: To exclude synagogues and houses of study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by giving the singular word a different job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גגך excludes בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות from the obligation of מעקה.

steps.title: רב ביבי rejects the rules: רבי אלעאי exempts partners from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי rejects רבא's rules by quoting a ברייתא in which רבי אלעאי exempts a partnership animal from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: These rules are not correct. A ברייתא teaches that an animal owned by partners is obligated in בכורה, but רבי אלעאי exempts it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא rejects the rules said earlier, which held that רבי אלעאי exempts partners only from ראשית הגז. He brings a ברייתא showing that רבי אלעאי exempts partners from בכורה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had limited רבי אלעאי's exemption for partners to ראשית הגז alone. This ברייתא shows that רבי אלעאי holds the same exemption for בכורה. So the rule 'only ראשית הגז' cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: These rules are not correct (literally: these rules do not exist)
An animal owned jointly by partners
The holiness of a firstborn animal
Exempts it

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
These rules are not correct,
phrases.notes: He means the rules רבא gave earlier, that רבי אלעאי exempts partners only from ראשית הגז.

phrases.english: as it is taught: An animal of partners
is obligated in firstborn status,
phrases.notes: Its firstborn offspring becomes a בכור.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Ilai exempts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the singular-verse discussion to rejecting רבא's rules about רבי אלעאי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's rule that רבי אלעאי exempts partners only from ראשית הגז
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעאי also exempts partners from בכורה.

steps.title: What is רבי אלעאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעאי's exemption from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for רבי אלעאי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעאי exempts a partnership animal from בכורה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave only רבי אלעאי's ruling, not his reason. The גמרא wants to find the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Ilai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי אלעאי's exemption of partners from בכורה.

steps.title: The singular 'בקרך וצאנך' means a single owner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'your herd and your flock' in the singular, which shows only an animal with one owner is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written 'your (singular) herd and your flock.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעאי learns his view from the singular word 'your' in the פסוק about בכורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בקרך' and 'צאנך' are singular forms, meaning 'your herd' belonging to one person. רבי אלעאי reads this as excluding an animal owned by partners. This is the same style of reading as the singular words discussed in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Your (singular) herd and your flock

phrases.english: As it is written: "Your herd and your flock,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17. 'Your' is singular here, and that is the whole point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'בקרך וצאנך' limits בכורה to an animal with one owner.

steps.title: But another פסוק says it in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: another פסוק says 'בקרכם וצאנכם' in the plural, which seems to include partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is also written 'your (plural) herd and your flock'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעאי's source. Another פסוק uses the plural 'your', which sounds like it includes animals owned together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the singular word excludes partners, then the plural word should include them. The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other, so the singular word alone cannot prove the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (introduces a challenge from another פסוק)
Your (plural) herd and your flock

phrases.english: But it is written: "Your herd and your flock"!
phrases.notes: דברים 12:6. Here 'your' is plural, the opposite of the פסוק just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the singular 'בקרך וצאנך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural form of the same phrase appears elsewhere, which suggests partners are included.

steps.title: The plural refers to all of the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The plural פסוק is speaking to the whole Jewish people, each with his own animals, not to partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: That plural is about all of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plural form is used because the פסוק is talking to the whole nation together. It does not mean animals owned in partnership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'your' addresses many people, each bringing his own firstborn. It does not describe one animal that several people own together. So the singular פסוק still teaches that a partnership animal is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Of all the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעאי, a partnership animal is exempt from בכורה because of the singular 'בקרך וצאנך'. The plural פסוק just speaks to the whole nation.

phrases.english: That refers to all of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the plural פסוק as addressing the whole nation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural form includes animals owned in partnership.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural speaks to all of Israel as individuals, so the singular still excludes partners.

steps.title: רב חנינא מסורא: רבי אלעאי exempts partners from מתנות
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא also rejects the rules, quoting a ברייתא where רבי אלעאי exempts a partnership animal from the priestly gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא מסורא said: These rules are not correct. A ברייתא teaches that an animal owned by partners is obligated in מתנות, but רבי אלעאי exempts it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא also rejects רבא's rules. He brings a different ברייתא showing that רבי אלעאי exempts partners from מתנות (the foreleg, cheeks and stomach given to a כהן).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second piece of evidence against the idea that רבי אלעאי exempts partners only from ראשית הגז. This time the topic is מתנות, not בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the cheeks and the stomach
Exempts

phrases.english: Rav Chanina of Sura said:
These rules are not correct,
as it is taught: An animal of partners is obligated in the gifts,
and Rabbi Ilai exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: לֵיתַנְהוּ לְהָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rejection of the same rules, using a different ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's rule that רבי אלעאי exempts partners only from ראשית הגז
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעאי also exempts partners from מתנות.

steps.title: Why does רבי אלעאי exempt partners from מתנות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעאי's exemption from מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעאי learns that partners are exempt from מתנות. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike בכורה, the פסוק about מתנות has no singular 'your' to point to. So the גמרא needs a different source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי אלעאי's exemption of partners from מתנות.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה of 'giving' from ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי learns from the shared word 'נתינה' that מתנות work like ראשית הגז, where partners are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'giving' and 'giving' from ראשית הגז: just as there partnership is not obligated, so too here partnership is not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'give' appears both by מתנות and by ראשית הגז, so they share the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי already exempts partners from ראשית הגז. Because the Torah uses the word 'give' for both מצוות, he carries that exemption over to מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns from the shared word 'giving' (a גזירה שוה)
The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
Just as there... so too here (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: He learns "giving" and "giving" from the first shearing –
phrases.notes: The word 'give' appears by מתנות (דברים 18:3) and by ראשית הגז (דברים 18:4).

phrases.english: just as there, partnership is not obligated,
so too here, partnership is not obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'נתינה' from ראשית הגז, where partners are exempt.

steps.title: If תרומה obligated partners, we would learn from תרומה instead
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא argues: if רבי אלעאי held partners are obligated in תרומה, the גזירה שוה could just as well come from תרומה and make partners obligated in מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that partners are obligated in תרומה, let us learn 'giving' and 'giving' from תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא tests רבא's claim that רבי אלעאי obligates partners in תרומה. He shows that this claim causes a problem for the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'give' also appears by תרומה. If partners were obligated in תרומה, we could compare מתנות to תרומה and obligate partners in מתנות, which is the opposite of the ברייתא. The ברייתא learns only an exemption, so this hypothetical runs into trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (introduces a hypothetical that will be rejected)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Let us learn

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real suggestion to learn from תרומה. It is a 'what if' that shows רבא's claim about תרומה cannot be right.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that partnership is obligated in תרומה,
let us learn "giving" and "giving" from תרומה!
phrases.notes: תרומה also uses the word 'give' (דברים 18:4), so it could have been the comparison instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the גזירה שוה of step 28 to test רבא's claim about תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעאי obligates partners in תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, 'נתינה' could be learned from תרומה, which would obligate partners in מתנות, against the ברייתא.

steps.title: So רבי אלעאי exempts partners from תרומה too
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion is that רבי אלעאי also exempts partners from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that he exempts in תרומה as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא concludes that רבי אלעאי exempts partners from תרומה as well, so רבא's rules are rejected here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once תרומה also exempts partners, it does not matter whether we learn מתנות from ראשית הגז or from תרומה. Either way, partners are exempt. This removes another part of רבא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, learn from this (introduces a conclusion)
Also

steps.whatToRemember: According to these two אמוראים, רבי אלעאי exempts partners not only from ראשית הגז but also from בכורה, מתנות and תרומה. This rejects רבא's rules.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that in תרומה he also exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בִּתְרוּמָה נָמֵי פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the hypothetical in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעאי exempts partners from תרומה as well, so רבא's rules are not accepted.

steps.title: If compared to תרומה, should מתנות apply only in ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link to תרומה: if מתנות learn from תרומה, they should apply only in ארץ ישראל, just like תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you compare them to תרומה, then just as תרומה applies in ארץ ישראל but not outside it, so too מתנות should apply in ארץ ישראל but not outside it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison to תרומה one step further. It points out a result that seems surprising: מתנות would apply only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 linked רבי אלעאי's rule on partners to תרומה. But once you compare two things, the comparison usually carries other rules along with it. Since תרומה from the Torah applies only in ארץ ישראל, the same limit should apply to מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
The priestly gifts from an animal: the foreleg, the jaw and the stomach
Outside ארץ ישראל
'If, just as…': opens a challenge that pushes a comparison further

phrases.english: If so, just as with תרומה,
in the Land, yes; outside the Land, no,
so too the priestly gifts:
in the Land, yes; outside the Land, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה, בָּאָרֶץ – אִין, בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רבי אלעאי compares the gifts to תרומה, and draws a further result from that comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between מתנות and תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison should carry over all of תרומה's rules, including that it applies only in ארץ ישראל. That result seems hard to accept.

steps.title: רבי יוסי מנהרביל accepts it: רבי אלעאי says so explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי מנהרביל says yes, that is correct. He cites a ברייתא where רבי אלעאי rules that both מתנות and ראשית הגז apply only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי of נהרביל said: Yes, that is right. And it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעאי says the gifts apply only in the Land. And likewise רבי אלעאי would say: ראשית הגז applies only in the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of fighting the challenge, רבי יוסי מנהרביל accepts it. He shows from a ברייתא that רבי אלעאי really holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What looked like a difficulty turns out to be רבי אלעאי's actual opinion. The ברייתא also adds that ראשית הגז is limited to ארץ ישראל. This sets up the next question: what is the source for that?

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing of wool, which is given to a כהן
Apply, are in effect
Yes (in רבי יוסי's reply)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אין' shows up twice with two different meanings. In 'אמר… אין' it means 'yes'. In 'אין נוהגין' it means 'do not'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei of Neharbil said: Yes, [indeed so],
and it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Ilai says:
the priestly gifts apply only in the Land,
phrases.notes: Here the same letters mean 'not' (אֵין). It is not the 'yes' from the line before.

phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Ilai would say:

phrases.aramaic: רֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז אִין נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: the first shearing applies only in the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִנְּהַרְבִּיל: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31 by accepting it and backing it up with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge as the actual הלכה, with support from a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Limiting מתנות to ארץ ישראל seemed like an absurd result
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעאי really does hold that מתנות and ראשית הגז apply only in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: What is רבי אלעאי's source for ראשית הגז?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעאי limits ראשית הגז to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אלעאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעאי's second ruling, about ראשית הגז. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now understand why מתנות are limited: they are compared directly to תרומה, which applies only in ארץ ישראל. But the ברייתא also limits ראשית הגז to ארץ ישראל, and that ruling still needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Ilai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ראשית הגז ruling cited in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for limiting ראשית הגז to ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רבא: ראשית הגז is learned from תרומה through the word 'giving'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי אלעאי learns ראשית הגז from תרומה through the shared word 'נתינה'. So like תרומה, it applies only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He learns 'giving' and 'giving' from תרומה. Just as תרומה applies in the Land and not outside it, so too ראשית הגז applies in the Land and not outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source. A גזירה שוה connects ראשית הגז to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'give' appears with both תרומה and ראשית הגז. That shared word links them, so ראשית הגז takes on תרומה's limit to ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns or derives
'Giving': the shared word that links the two topics
Learning one law from another through a shared word in the פסוקים

phrases.english: Rava said:
He learns 'giving' and 'giving' from תרומה:
phrases.notes: Both תרומה and ראשית הגז appear with 'תתן לו' in דברים 18:4.

phrases.aramaic: מָה תְּרוּמָה, בָּאָרֶץ – אִין, בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ – לָא,
phrases.english: just as תרומה applies in the Land, yes, but outside the Land, no,

phrases.aramaic: אַף רֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז, בָּאָרֶץ – אִין, בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ – לָא.
phrases.english: so too the first shearing: in the Land, yes; outside the Land, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: יָלֵיף נְתִינָה נְתִינָה מִתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'נתינה' links ראשית הגז to תרומה, which applies only in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: אביי: Should ראשית הגז make the wool forbidden like טבל?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if ראשית הגז is compared to תרומה, it should also make the wool forbidden as טבל until it is separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, just as תרומה makes produce טבל, should ראשית הגז also make wool like טבל?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests how far רבא's comparison goes. He points to another rule of תרומה that does not seem to apply to wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce is forbidden to eat until its תרומה is taken off. This is called טבל. If ראשית הגז is fully like תרומה, then wool should be forbidden to use until its portion is set aside. Yet that is not the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes something into טבל
Produce that is forbidden because its gifts have not yet been separated

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so, just as תרומה creates טבל status,
phrases.notes: Produce stays forbidden until its תרומה is set aside.

phrases.english: should the first shearing also create טבל status?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה טוֹבֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's גזירה שוה from step 34 by asking whether it carries too much over.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's comparison of ראשית הגז to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would make the wool טבל, which is not the הלכה

steps.title: The פסוק limits the כהן's share to the moment it is set aside
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the פסוק that the כהן has a share only from the moment the ראשית is set aside. So the rest of the wool is never forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The פסוק says 'And the first shearing of your flock you shall give him'. You have a share in it only from its being made 'first' and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא blocks אביי's challenge by pointing to the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ראשית גז' shows that the כהן's right begins only once the portion is designated. Before that, the wool has nothing of the כהן's in it, so nothing makes it forbidden. The comparison to תרומה still stands, but this rule is an exception to it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the point it becomes 'first' (is set aside) onward

phrases.english: He said to him: The verse states:
'And the first shearing of your flock you shall give him'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: you [the כהן] have nothing in it
except from its becoming 'first' and onward.
phrases.notes: The כהן owns nothing until the portion is actually set aside, so the rest of the wool is never forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אָמַר קְרָא וְרֵאשִׁית גֵּז צֹאנְךָ תִּתֶּן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראשית הגז would make the wool forbidden like טבל
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן's share begins only once it is set aside, so the wool is not טבל

steps.title: אביי: Should ראשית הגז carry מיתה and חומש like תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again: a non-כהן who eats תרומה is liable to מיתה or חומש. Should the same apply to ראשית הגז?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as one is liable for מיתה and חומש over תרומה, should one also be liable for מיתה and חומש over ראשית הגז?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises a second test of the comparison. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, a non-כהן who eats it on purpose gets מיתה at the hands of Heaven. One who eats it by mistake pays back an extra fifth (חומש). If ראשית הגז is like תרומה, the same penalties should apply, yet there is no such rule for wool.

keyTerms.meaning: Death at the hands of Heaven, for a non-כהן who eats תרומה on purpose
An extra fifth paid by a non-כהן who eats תרומה by mistake
A non-כהן

phrases.english: If so, just as with תרומה
one is liable over it to death and the [added] fifth,
phrases.notes: A non-כהן who eats it on purpose gets מיתה from Heaven. If he eats it by mistake, he pays an extra fifth.

phrases.english: so too the first shearing:
should one be liable over it to death and the fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה חַיָּיבִים עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה וָחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 36 answered the טבל challenge, אביי raises a second challenge against the same comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's comparison of ראשית הגז to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would bring תרומה's penalties of מיתה and חומש over to wool, which is not the הלכה

steps.title: No death penalty or extra fifth for ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the פסוקים about תרומה. The words 'בו' and 'עליו' limit death and חומש to תרומה only, not ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'and die because of it' and 'he shall add to it.' 'To it' means to תרומה and not to ראשית הגז. 'Because of it' means because of תרומה and not because of ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge from step 37. He shows that the פסוק itself limits death and the extra fifth to תרומה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison through 'נתינה' brings over some rules of תרומה, but not every rule. The small words 'בו' (because of it) and 'עליו' (to it) point only at תרומה. So a non-כהן who uses ראשית הגז gets neither מיתה nor חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will die because of it: the death penalty from Heaven for a non-כהן who eats תרומה
And he shall add to it: the extra fifth (חומש) paid for eating תרומה by mistake
An extra fifth added to the payment

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And die because of it,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:9

phrases.english: 'and he shall add to it' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:14

phrases.english: 'to it,' and not to the first shearing,
'because of it,' and not because of the first shearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וּמֵתוּ בוֹ, וְיָסַף עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge about מיתה and חומש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to תרומה should bring over the death penalty and the extra fifth too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'בו' and 'עליו' limit those penalties to תרומה alone.

steps.title: Should tithes follow ראשית הגז like they follow תרומה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again: after תרומה come מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, so the same should be true after ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as with תרומה a first tithe and second tithe come after it, so too with ראשית הגז a first and second tithe should come after it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings another rule of תרומה and asks if it should also apply to ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With produce, after you separate תרומה you still have to separate מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני. If ראשית הגז is like תרומה, maybe wool also needs more separations after it.

keyTerms.meaning: If [it is like that], then just as... — opening a comparison challenge
First and second: מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני
After it

phrases.english: If so, just as with תרומה
a first and a second come after it,
phrases.notes: He means מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, which are taken after תרומה.

phrases.english: so too the first shearing
should have a first and a second after it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי אַחֲרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge in the same series against the תרומה comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's comparison of ראשית הגז to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is real, the tithes that follow תרומה should also follow ראשית הגז.

steps.title: Only one separation for ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the word 'ראשית' teaches there is only the first gift and nothing after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'first.' You have nothing in it except the first gift alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge about tithes. He says the פסוק calls it only 'ראשית', the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ראשית' shows that ראשית הגז has just one gift. So the tithes that come after תרומה do not carry over to wool.

keyTerms.meaning: First, the first portion
Only, alone

phrases.english: The verse states 'first,'
you have nothing in it
except the first alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא רֵאשִׁית, אֵין לְךָ בּוֹ אֶלָּא רֵאשִׁית בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about tithes after ראשית הגז.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Like תרומה, ראשית הגז should be followed by more tithes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'ראשית' means only one gift, with nothing after it.

steps.title: Can you give from new wool for old wool
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: with תרומה you cannot give from new produce for old produce. Is the same true for ראשית הגז?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as with תרומה you may not give from the new for the old, so too with ראשית הגז you may not give from the new for the old?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings one more rule of תרומה and asks if it carries over to ראשית הגז. This time רבא will agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, you cannot separate from this year's crop to cover last year's crop. If ראשית הגז is like תרומה, then this year's wool could not cover last year's wool either.

keyTerms.meaning: From the new for the old: giving from this year's produce to cover last year's

phrases.english: If so, just as with תרומה,
from the new for the old – no,
phrases.notes: New and old here mean this year's crop and last year's crop.

phrases.english: so too the first shearing,
from the new for the old – no?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה, מֵחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another test of how far the תרומה comparison reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the comparison between ראשית הגז and תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison holds, the ban on new-for-old in תרומה should apply to wool too.

steps.title: רבא agrees: no new for old
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers 'yes': ראשית הגז also cannot be given from new wool for old wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: This time רבא does not push back. He agrees that this rule of תרומה does apply to ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike death, חומש and tithes, there is no פסוק here that blocks the comparison. So the rule carries over: new wool cannot cover old wool.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבא rejects every one of אביי's challenges. Here he agrees, so this rule of תרומה really does apply to ראשית הגז.

phrases.english: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point raised in step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether new wool can be given for old wool
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; like תרומה, ראשית הגז cannot be given from new for old.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the challenger's comparison is accepted
steps.terutzMaskana: Like תרומה, ראשית הגז cannot be given from new wool for old wool

steps.title: A ברייתא about wool shorn over several years
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought: wool from two sheep collected over two or three years does not combine, which implies wool from five sheep does combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: Someone had two sheep. He sheared and put it aside, sheared and put it aside, for two or three years. The wool does not combine. This implies that with five sheep, it does combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא connected to רבא's 'yes' about new and old wool. This begins a proof that will continue in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sheep do not count, even if their wool over several years adds up to a lot. The inference is that five sheep do count, even when the wool was shorn in different years. This ברייתא is the first side of a comparison the גמרא is about to develop.

keyTerms.meaning: Ewes, sheep
He sheared and put [the wool] aside
They combine to reach the minimum amount

phrases.english: And it is taught:
If he had two sheep,
he sheared and put it aside, sheared and put it aside,
for two or three years –
they do not combine.
This implies that five do combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to רבא's agreement about new and old wool.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling about new and old wool for ראשית הגז
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two sheep shorn over several years, with its inference about five sheep

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the wool does not combine
steps.stepSummary: Against the inference from the previous ברייתא, the גמרא cites another ברייתא saying wool from different years does not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that the wool does not combine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the opposite of what we just inferred: wool shorn in different years does not combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the last ברייתא we inferred that wool from five sheep, shorn over several years, does combine. This new ברייתא says even such wool does not combine. Now two ברייתות contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: combine; add up together to reach the required amount

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: they do not combine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference drawn from the ברייתא in step 43
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that wool from five sheep over several years combines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא rules directly that such wool does not combine, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא that says the wool does not combine follows רבי אלעאי, and the one that says it combines follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: this one follows רבי אלעאי, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי compares ראשית הגז to תרומה. Just as you cannot give תרומה from new produce for old, wool from different years does not combine. The רבנן do not make this comparison, so for them wool from different years does combine.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this; conclude from it
the Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Not combining wool from different years is רבי אלעאי's view, because he treats ראשית הגז like תרומה. The רבנן let it combine.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this:
this one follows רבי אלעאי,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the wool does not combine, because he compares ראשית הגז to תרומה.

phrases.english: and that one follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 44
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to give one rule and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Not combining is רבי אלעאי's view, based on comparing to תרומה. Combining is the view of the רבנן.

steps.title: Should wool that grew under a גוי be exempt, like תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes the comparison to תרומה further. Produce that grew while it was exempt stays exempt, so wool that grew while a גוי owned the sheep should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you compare to תרומה: just as with תרומה, what grew under obligation is obligated and what grew under exemption is exempt, so too with ראשית הגז, what grew under obligation is obligated and what grew under exemption is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks whether another rule of תרומה should carry over to ראשית הגז: what grew while it was exempt stays exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Jew buys produce that grew while a גוי owned it, that growth is exempt from תרומה. If ראשית הגז is like תרומה, wool that grew while a גוי owned the sheep should stay exempt even after a Jew buys them.

keyTerms.meaning: grew while under obligation (owned by a Jew)
grew while exempt (owned by a גוי)
the first shearing, a gift of wool given to the כהן

phrases.english: If, just as with תרומה,
what grew under obligation is obligated,
what grew under exemption is exempt,
so too the first shearing as well:
what grew under obligation is obligated,
what grew under exemption is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the same comparison to תרומה over to a new rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעאי's comparison of ראשית הגז to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison holds, the exemption for growth under a גוי's ownership should carry over to wool as well.

steps.title: The source for the תרומה rule: a field bought from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows where we learn the תרומה rule: a ברייתא about a Jew who buys a field in סוריא from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for תרומה, how do we know this? As it is taught: A Jew who bought a field in סוריא from a גוי, before it reached one-third of its growth, is obligated. After it reached one-third, רבי עקיבא obligates him on the added growth, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the source that proves the תרומה rule he is relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jew bought the field before the crop reached one-third of its growth, the produce counts as grown under him, so he is obligated. If he bought it after, רבי עקיבא obligates only the extra growth, and the חכמים exempt it all. Either way, the growth that happened while the גוי owned it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?
Syria, land conquered next to ארץ ישראל
one-third, the stage of growth where produce counts as grown
the extra growth added after the purchase

phrases.english: And regarding תרומה, from where do we know this?
As it is taught: A Jew who bought a field
in סוריא from a גוי,
before it reached one-third of its growth, he is obligated,
after it reached one-third of its growth,
רבי עקיבא obligates him on the added growth,
and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the תרומה rule used in step 46
steps.raayaObject: The rule that produce that grew under a גוי's ownership is exempt from תרומה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a Jew who buys a field in סוריא from a גוי

steps.title: Our משנה obligates sheep bought ready for shearing
steps.stepSummary: If you say רבי אלעאי does hold that wool grown under a גוי is exempt, our משנה contradicts this. Buying the fleece is exempt, which implies buying the sheep for shearing is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, didn't we learn: One who buys the fleece of a גוי's sheep is exempt from ראשית הגז. This implies that if he bought his sheep for shearing, he is obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes off the easy answer, 'yes, it is exempt,' by pointing to our משנה, which seems to obligate wool that grew under a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says buying only the fleece is exempt. That implies buying the sheep themselves, ready to be shorn, is obligated, even though that wool grew while the גוי owned them. So for wool, growth under a גוי does not seem to exempt, unlike תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you say, indeed so
wool/fleece, here bought while still attached
to shear; ready for shearing

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: you might answer that רבי אלעאי really does exempt wool that grew while a גוי owned the sheep.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn: One who buys the fleece of a גוי's sheep
is exempt from the first shearing,
which implies that if he bought his sheep for shearing, he is obligated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the comparison from step 46 cannot simply be accepted, because the משנה says otherwise
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that wool grown under a גוי's ownership is exempt for רבי אלעאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that buying a גוי's sheep for shearing creates an obligation, even though the wool grew while the גוי owned them.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer about the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts his reply with the word 'מתניתין'. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening word of רבא's answer. The גמרא is setting up his explanation of how the משנה fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By opening with 'the משנה,' רבא shows he will deal directly with the משנה that אביי quoted. Most likely he will say whose opinion it follows. The full answer comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה

phrases.english: Our משנה...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to אביי's challenge from the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה (continues in the next lines)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to contradict רבי אלעאי
steps.terutzMaskana: The explanation follows in the continuation of the text
